children: A wholly owned subsidiary of Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) has been named as one of the investors in the Indian government backed $2 billion NIIF Infrastructure Fund II.

Singapore’s Temasek, Canada’s CPP Investments, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, AustralianSuper, alongside Indian institutions including ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Life Insurance and HDFC Life Insurance have invested in India’s sovereign-anchored alternative asset manager National Investment and Infrastructure Fund Limited (NIIF).
Financial details have not been disclosed.
Alongside the Fund, NIIF aims to mobilise $950 million in co-investment capital, enabling investors to participate at scale in select transactions.
The first close represents over 60% of the fund’s $3.2 billion target size, which focuses on infrastructure sectors including energy, transport, digital, urban and electric mobility.
(Writing by Bindu Rai, editing by Seban Scaria)

title: ADIA unit invests in India’s $2bln NIIF infrastructure fund
